title: I returned this one the day that I got it.
text: I returned this one the day that I got it.. I return this product the day that I got it. It didn’t take long for me to realize I would never like this type of clock. I thought maybe the atomic feature would be a fun option to have, but with this clock it was an all day annoyance. I understood that it may not connect with the radio waves that it takes for the atomic feature to kick in, but once I manually said the time, the clock kept searching for the radio waves on its own. The overall clock is a lot smaller than it looks in the picture too. I’m just not happy with this style o’clock. Others may have good luck with it but I didn’t.

product_metadata.title: Sharp Desktop Dual Alarm Clock with Color Display - Atomic Accuracy - Calendar & Day of Week Time/Date Display
features: Color Atomic Alarm Clock - Accurate to the Second! The Atomic Clock has a built in receiver that automatically synchronizes itself with the WWVB radio broadcast by the US Government’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in Fort Collins, Colorado. The Atomic Clock will always be accurate to within on second as it receives daily WWVB updates.

Color Calendar and Day of Week Display - Always know what day of the week it is with a quick glance. The clock displays the calendar and the day of the week. Using the Snooze/Dimmer switch on top of the display, you can easily adjust the display brightness to your liking.
EASY TO SET DUAL ALARM - Set alarm for two people, or set one alarm for weekdays and the other for weekend!. Snooze/Dimmer Switch is simple to use and on top of the display.

BATTERY BACK-UP - There is a "No Worry" battery back-up option (requires 2 x AAA battery, sold separately), that will allow the alarm to go off, even if the power goes out. The battery back-up stores the time and alarm settings if the power is interrupted. During battery back-up the clock’s display will not be lit. Once power is restored, the display will re-light.

ALWAYS ON DISPLAY – Display is always illuminated. You can use the Snooze/Dimmer switch on top of the display, to easily adjust the display brightness to your liking. NOTE: The screen will go dark while the clock is setting and searching for the Atomic Signal. Once signal is located, the screen will always be illuminated.
